title: US investigates whether Iran is behind cyberattacks and bomb threats against tankers, ynet reports citing WSJ
date_note: Al-Monitor and Fox News, both published 23 November, cite the Wall Street Journal report of that Monday; ynet and LSM relayed it on 24 November. Attacks cited include September ones.
geo_basis: United States, where the investigation and the Coast Guard response are reported; the ships' locations vary
summary: Ynet, Al-Monitor and LSM, relaying a Wall Street Journal report, say US officials are investigating whether Iran, or possibly Russia, is behind cyberattacks on tankers; LSM adds Russia's possible responsibility has not been ruled out. Ynet adds a Trump administration official said there was no evidence yet. Fox News says a Coast Guard spokesperson confirmed cyber teams boarded two foreign-flagged ships in August; Iran was not named.
plain: Ynet, citing the Wall Street Journal, says US officials are investigating whether Iran is behind dozens of cyberattacks on energy tankers. Ynet says a Trump administration official said there is no evidence yet.
exec: Ynet reports the US is investigating cyberattacks and bomb threats on tankers, some bound for US ports; Iran is the main suspect, not confirmed.
action: No action needed; for awareness. The report says the US Coast Guard urges shipping companies to report suspicious activity and use its free resources.

evidence.quote: The offshore operations took place Aug. 21 and 24 in the Gulf of America

validation.note: Two publishers read (ynet, Hebrew; Al-Monitor relaying Reuters), both relaying one Wall Street Journal report that was not read, so the core fact is single-origin. Al-Monitor says Reuters could not immediately verify the report. Fox News (read) quotes a Coast Guard spokesperson confirming the boardings; its account of the attacks also relays the Wall Street Journal. LSM (24 Nov) also relays the WSJ report (up to 50 ships; Russia not ruled out); it is the same single origin.

review.note: date: WSJ report and Al-Monitor/Fox are 23 Nov, not 24; exec oil and gas ships changed to tankers
